en: The Bodhisattvapiṭaka Sūtra, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Saṃghabara of Funan during the Liang Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
Together with a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus and seventy-two thousand bodhisattvas,

at that time the Elder Śāriputra, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms in homage to the Buddha, and addressed the Buddha, saying: “World-Honored One!”
"How do sons and daughters of good family repent to extinguish their offenses and swiftly attain *samyaksambodhi*?
The Buddha told Śāriputra:

"Whether it be those who wish to study *samyaksambodhi*, or followers of the Śrāvaka vehicle, or followers of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle, or followers of the Mahāyāna, or other sentient beings, they should recite the names of the ten Buddhas of the ten worlds in the ten directions. They should light ten thousand lamps—using either ghee or oil—and provide incense and powdered incense in numbers corresponding to the lamps. They should also offer various flowers, various fruits, and various leaves as a great offering and practice great generosity."

Fill ten *piṅga* vessels with water and ten *kāṃsa* bowls with water; bathe until pure, perfume the body with incense, and put on fresh, clean garments. Wash the hands and feet once more, holding ten lotus flowers in each hand. One should subsist on a vegetarian diet, and ensure that all attendants and servants are likewise clean and pure.

In each of the ten directions, one should provide seats for the Buddhas; the central Buddha seat above should be slightly higher. The person performing the repentance should arrange seats as convenient in the ten directions, and while seated, pay homage to the Buddhas of the ten directions. They should personally confess and reveal all karmic actions committed from the past, as well as the multitude of evils created since beginningless birth and death, resolving to reform the past and cultivate the future, vowing never to commit them again!
The Buddha said, “Śāriputra!
In the eastern direction there is a world named Aśoka, which means ‘Sorrowless. In that place there is a Buddha named Candravijaya.”
In the southern direction is the world Nanda, which means "Joy"; there dwells a Buddha named Candanagiri.
In the western direction is the world Bhadra, which means "Virtuous"; there dwells a Buddha named Anantaprabha.
In the northern direction is the world Ālokacakṣus, which means "Beneficial Eye"; there dwells a Buddha named Dhvajagiri.
In the southeastern direction, in the world Moonlight, there is a Buddha named Vigataśoka;
in the southwestern direction, in the world Banner, there is a Buddha named Ratnakṣetra;
in the northwestern direction, in the world Resounding, there is a Buddha named Puṣpaguṇa.
In the northeast, in the world of Peaceful Security, there is a Buddha named Tri-vīrya;
in the zenith, in the world of Moon, there is a Buddha named Mahā-guṇa-śrī;
and in the nadir, in the world of Great Fame, there is a Buddha named Prabhā-śrī.

For one day and one night, during the six periods, he practiced the Way and paid homage, baring his right shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, and with palms joined toward the Buddha, spoke these words:

"I pay homage to all Buddhas, Tathāgatas—those present Buddhas of the ten directions who have already attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, who are currently turning the wheel of Dharma, manifesting the wheel of Dharma, manifesting the taking up of the wheel of Dharma, manifesting the raining down of the rain of Dharma, manifesting the beating of the drum of Dharma, manifesting the blowing of the conch of Dharma, manifesting the erecting of the banner of Dharma, manifesting the lighting of the torch of Dharma, and who are currently satisfying sentient beings with the gift of Dharma, preaching for them according to their inclinations, bringing great benefit and peace to sentient beings, acting out of compassion for the world, and acting for the welfare of the multitudes of devas and humans; I now prostrate my head in homage to those Tathāgatas."
Those Tathāgatas and those Buddhas are worthy of honor; they should be venerated with offerings.
These Buddhas possess great wisdom and are the eyes of the world; they are able to bear witness for the world, presiding over the world, knowing it directly and seeing it directly.
With body, speech, and mind, I pay homage to that Buddha.
"Whatever evil karma I have created since beginningless birth and death has served as an obstacle for all sentient beings;
whether through the arising of greed, the arising of anger, or the arising of delusion, I failed to recognize the Buddha and the Dharma."
...or a monk who, being ignorant of wholesome and unwholesome dharmas, sheds the blood of a Buddha with evil body, speech, or mind;
or slanders the True Dharma; or breaks the harmony of the Saṃgha; or kills a true person, an Arhat;
or kills one's father or mother; or fully engages in the ten unwholesome paths of action; or has already committed [them]...
Whether they have committed them in the present, will commit them in the future, or see others committing them and rejoice in them with praise;
or whether they create various evils through the three actions of body, four of speech, and three of mind; or speak harshly, revile, and slander others;
or deceive people with false measures and scales; or are born into the six realms of existence and afflict their parents.
Or they may take property from stupas or monasteries, or use the property of the Sangha, or the property of the Sangha from the four quarters;
or they may violate the precepts established by the Buddha, or fail to follow the instructions of their preceptors and acharyas;
or they may become angry or abusive, or slander the Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Mahāyāna; or, driven by stinginess and jealousy, they may commit various evils.
Whether I have reviled the Tathāgatas with harsh abuse, or spoken of the Dharma as non-Dharma, or spoken of non-Dharma as Dharma—
all such evils as these, I now confess and repent before the Buddhas of the ten directions!
Those Tathāgatas see me directly, know me directly, and realize me directly; before these Buddhas, I reveal my transgressions with a single mind, not daring to conceal them;
having revealed them, I vow never to commit them again.

These various karmic offenses should lead to rebirth in the realms of hell, hungry ghosts, animals, or asuras, or to passing through the eight difficult conditions; I vow that these offenses shall be extinguished before me now and never arise again in the future!
"Today, in the presence of all Buddhas, I openly confess and repent, not daring to conceal anything;
having confessed, I vow never to commit such acts again."

Just as the bodhisattvas of the past, for the sake of practicing enlightenment, performed repentance in such a manner, I now likewise repent of my karmic obstructions; having confessed them, I dare not commit them again.
Just as the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the future shall perform repentance, I likewise repent and confess; having confessed them, I vow never to do so again.

Just as the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the present in the ten directions, for the sake of practicing enlightenment, are currently performing repentance, I likewise repent and confess, vowing never to do so again.

Just as all Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the three periods—past, future, and present—have repented, shall repent, and are currently repenting for the sake of practicing bodhi, I likewise repent; I vow never again to commit such acts.
"Śāriputra! If good men or good women should repent in this manner.
For this reason, Śāriputra!"
If good sons or good daughters wish to attain purity in all dharmas without any obstruction, they should perform repentance for their various evil karmic obstructions in this manner;
having confessed them, they must vow never to commit them again.

If one wishes to be born into the Kṣatriya caste or a wealthy and noble lineage, possessing abundant treasures and all manner of endowments, with a handsome appearance, and desires to attain the Mahāyāna, one should perform repentance in this way;
if one wishes to attain the realm of the Four Heavenly Kings, one should perform repentance in this way;
if one wishes to attain the Heaven of the Thirty-three, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, or the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, one should perform repentance in this way.

If one wishes to attain birth among the Brahmakāyika devas, the Brahmapurohita devas, the Mahābrahmā devas, the Parīttābha, the Apramāṇābha, the Ābhāsvara, the Parīttaśubha, the Apramāṇaśubha, the Śubhakṛtsna, the Bṛhatphala, the Avṛha, the Atapa, the Sudṛśa, the Sudarśana, or the Akaniṣṭha devas, one should perform repentance in this manner.

If you wish to be reborn in the formless realms—the sphere of infinite space, the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, or the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception—you should repent in this manner.
If you wish to attain the fruits of a srotāpanna, sakṛdāgāmin, anāgāmin, or arhat, you should repent in this manner.
If you wish to attain the three knowledges (*traividya*), the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*), mastery over spiritual powers, and sharp, keen intelligence;
or if you wish to attain the enlightenment of a *pratyekabuddha*, you should perform repentance in this manner.

If you wish to attain all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), pure knowledge, inconceivable knowledge, unequaled knowledge, and perfect universal knowledge (*samyaksaṃbuddhajñāna*), you should likewise perform repentance in this way.
“Śāriputra! Why is this?

All phenomena arise from causes and conditions. As the Tathāgata has taught, there are phenomena that arise from conditions and phenomena that cease from conditions. Because causes and conditions proceed in succession, when those phenomena have passed, they have already ceased and already transformed; yet their karma remains unobstructed. Furthermore, regarding those phenomena that have not yet arisen, they too are without obstruction.”
Śāriputra! Why is this?
All dharmas spoken by the Tathāgata are entirely empty and quiescent; they are without sentient beings, without life-span, and without a person; they are neither born nor extinguished.
Śāriputra! All dharmas are created by oneself; moreover, this "self" itself also exists. Śāriputra!

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family wishes to enter this wisdom of the Dharma—namely, that there is no truly existent sentient being—this is called the teaching on the extinction of all karmic obstructions.
The Chapter on Repentance concludes.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

Good sons and good daughters who wish to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, or those who wish to attain the Śrāvaka-yāna, the Pratyekabuddha-yāna, or the Mahāyāna, as well as any other persons practicing meritorious deeds—how should they give rise to roots of goodness through sympathetic joy (*anumodanā*)?
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śāriputra:

“If good sons or good daughters wish to rejoice, they should, during the six periods of day and night, bare their right shoulders, place their right knees upon the ground, and with palms joined in reverence, speak these words:

‘If there are sentient beings in the ten directions who have already performed meritorious deeds—whether through giving, ethical discipline, or cultivation—I rejoice in all of them. With the foremost rejoicing, the supreme rejoicing, the most excellent rejoicing, the unsurpassed rejoicing, the peerless rejoicing, and the rejoicing equal to the unequaled, I rejoice in them all in this manner.’”

If there are sentient beings who shall perform meritorious deeds in the ten directions—whether through giving, or through observing the precepts, or through spiritual cultivation—I rejoice in all of them with the foremost rejoicing, the supreme rejoicing, the most excellent rejoicing, the unsurpassed rejoicing, the peerless rejoicing, and the rejoicing equal to the unequaled; I rejoice in them all in this manner.

If there are sentient beings in the ten directions who are currently performing meritorious deeds—whether through giving, observing precepts, or spiritual cultivation—I rejoice in all of them with the foremost rejoicing, the supreme rejoicing, the most excellent rejoicing, the unsurpassed rejoicing, the incomparable rejoicing, and the rejoicing equal to the unequaled; I rejoice in them all in this manner.

“Whatever merit those bodhisattvas have from their initial generation of the mind of awakening; whatever mass of merit those bodhisattvas have accumulated through cultivation for a hundred eons; whatever mass of merit those bodhisattvas have attained through the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*); whatever mass of merit those bodhisattvas have attained through the stage of non-retrogression (*avaivartika-bhūmi*); and whatever merit those bodhisattvas have from progressing sequentially through the ten stages (*bhūmi*)—I rejoice in all of that with the foremost rejoicing, the supreme rejoicing, and even the rejoicing equal to the unequaled (*asamasama*).”
If a bodhisattva has previously cultivated roots of goodness and merit associated with the six pāramitās, I rejoice in them all, with the foremost rejoicing, up to the peerless rejoicing.

If there are future bodhisattvas who shall practice the roots of goodness and meritorious virtues associated with the six pāramitās, I rejoice in them all, with the foremost rejoicing, up to the rejoicing that is equal to the unequaled.
I rejoice in all the merits associated with the practice of the six pāramitās by all bodhisattvas of the present, with the foremost rejoicing, up to the peerless rejoicing.

“I rejoice in all the merits accomplished by the past Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, who, having already attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and having turned the wheel of Dharma, acted for the benefit of sentient beings, for the peace and security of sentient beings, out of compassion for sentient beings, and for the sake of benefiting with righteousness sentient beings—including devas, humans, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas—as well as for the sake of devas and humans.”

I rejoice in all the merits performed by future Tathāgatas who shall attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and turn the wheel of Dharma for the benefit of sentient beings, for the peace and security of sentient beings, out of compassion for sentient beings, and for the sake of benefiting sentient beings through righteous principles; as well as the merits performed by devas, humans, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas, I rejoice in them all.

I rejoice in all the merits performed by the Buddhas of the ten directions who have now attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, who are now turning the wheel of Dharma, who are now kindling the torch of Dharma, who are now beating the drum of Dharma, who are now blowing the conch of Dharma, who are now erecting the banner of Dharma, and who are now satisfying, benefiting, and bringing peace to sentient beings through the gift of Dharma, showing compassion to the world and benefiting all humans and devas with righteous purpose—including those of the Śrāvaka, Pratyekabuddha, and Mahāyāna vehicles—with my foremost rejoicing, up to and including peerless rejoicing.
“Śāriputra! This is called the mass of merit from sympathetic joy (*anumodanā*).

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family practices this merit by means of this mass of merit from sympathetic joy, the fruit and retribution of this merit are incalculable and immeasurable.”

Śāriputra! If all sentient beings in a trichiliocosm, even as many as the sands of the Ganges River in worlds throughout the ten directions, were to exhaust their outflows and become arhats, and if some son or daughter of good family were to provide them with the four requisites for the rest of their lives—compared to the merit of a son or daughter of good family who rejoices in this [merit], the latter’s merit would be immeasurable and boundless, surpassing the former.

Therefore, Śāriputra, if a son of good family or a daughter of good family wishes to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, they should rejoice; if a woman wishes to obtain a male body, she should likewise rejoice.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One, you have already explained rejoicing for the sake of the illumination of bodhisattvas in the present and future; what, then, is the manner of exhortation?”
The Buddha told Śāriputra:

“If a son of good family or a daughter of good family desires to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi—whether by means of the Śrāvaka vehicle, the Pratyekabuddha vehicle, the Mahāyāna, or as any other sentient being—they should, during the six periods of day and night, bare their right shoulder, place their right knee on the ground, and with palms joined in reverence, speak these words:
‘I pay homage to all Buddhas, World-Honored Ones; to all Buddhas currently residing in the ten directions who have already attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and are now turning the wheel of Dharma.’”

I have already paid homage to those Buddhas; I now entreat them to turn the wheel of Dharma. May all Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, turn the wheel of Dharma! May they kindle the lamp of Dharma, open the eye of Dharma, and light the torch of Dharma! May they raise the clouds of Dharma, blow the conch of Dharma, beat the drum of Dharma, and erect the banner of Dharma! For the benefit of sentient beings, for the peace and security of sentient beings, out of compassion for the world, may they bring benefit through righteousness to all devas and humans!
"Śāriputra! Six times throughout the day and night, with the right shoulder bared, the right knee touching the ground, and palms joined in reverence, one should speak these words:

'I pay homage to all Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones. If any of the Buddhas of the ten directions intend to enter parinirvāṇa, I shall exhort those Buddhas, entreating them to remain long in the world for the benefit and peace of sentient beings, out of compassion for the world to bring welfare through righteousness to all devas and humans; for the sake of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, I perform this entreaty!'"
"Śāriputra! This is called the assembly of exhortation.
The merit obtained by good sons and good daughters through this assembly of exhortation is immeasurable."

Śāriputra! If a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to fill a trichiliocosm with the seven treasures and offer them as a gift to the Tathāgata, the merit of a son or daughter of good family who previously exhorted and requested [the turning of the wheel of Dharma] would surpass this merit by an immeasurable and boundless degree.

Śāriputra! If one were to fill worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges with the seven treasures and offer them as alms to the Buddhas, the merit of a son or daughter of good family who previously makes this exhortation would surpass that merit by an immeasurable and boundless degree.
Thus one entreats for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Śāriputra, such is my entreaty;
this is called the "assemblage of entreaty."
By means of this assembly of exhortations, if a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to manifest such exhortation now, their merit would be inconceivable. Why is this?

Śāriputra! When I was formerly practicing the bodhisattva conduct, I made such entreaties to the Buddhas to turn the wheel of Dharma. By virtue of this merit, I have attained anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. Śakra and the various devas, Brahmā, the Lord of the Sahā World, and others likewise entreated me to turn the wheel of Dharma, for the sake of bringing great benefit, peace, and security to the world, and even to benefit all gods and humans through its meaning.

Śāriputra! In the past, I exhorted and requested all Tathāgatas to cause the Dharma to abide for a long time. By virtue of these roots of merit, I have attained the ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, and the eighteen unique dharmas; I have attained the four unhindered analytical knowledges and great loving-kindness and great compassion. Now that I have entered nirvāṇa, my Dharma shall abide for a long time!
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

How should a son of good family or a daughter of good family who wishes to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*—whether belonging to the vehicle of the śrāvakas, the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas, the Great Vehicle, or other sentient beings—practice the dedication of roots of goodness for the sake of all-knowledge?”
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śāriputra:

"If a son of good family or a daughter of good family who desires to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi—whether they belong to the vehicle of the śrāvakas, the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas, the Mahāyāna, or any other sentient beings—should, during the six periods of day and night, bare their right shoulders, place their right knees upon the ground, and with palms joined in reverence, speak these words:"

"Whatever roots of merit and wholesome deeds I have performed throughout beginningless saṃsāra—whether toward the Buddha, the Dharma, or the Saṅgha; whether giving even a single morsel of food to a person or even to an animal; whether through repentance, entreaty, or sympathetic joy; or the merit of taking refuge in the Triple Gem and receiving the precepts—I now unite all of these and dedicate them for the benefit of all sentient beings. Just as the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, with their manifest wisdom and unattached wisdom, dedicate [their merit] to all sentient beings, I likewise dedicate it to all sentient beings."

Just as one who holds a precious jewel in their hand bestows it upon all, or as a cloud sends down rain to provide nourishment and benefit, so too may these merits be inexhaustible and undiminished—for the sake of the wealth and nobility of sentient beings, for the non-diminution of merit, the non-diminution of the Dharma, the non-diminution of wisdom, and the non-diminution of eloquence; for the sake of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and for the attainment of omniscience. I give these merits to all sentient beings; uniting them all, I dedicate them toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. By means of these roots of goodness, I vow that all sentient beings shall likewise attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and achieve omniscience.
"Just as the bodhisattvas of the past cultivated roots of goodness for the sake of awakening and dedicated them toward omniscience;
so too do I dedicate these roots of goodness toward omniscience, that by these roots of goodness I may attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening and realize omniscience."
Just as all bodhisattvas of the future shall practice the dedication of roots of goodness for the sake of omniscience,
so too do I dedicate my roots of goodness for the sake of omniscience.
Just as the bodhisattvas of the present cultivate roots of goodness for the sake of all-knowledge,
so too do I dedicate these roots of goodness for the sake of all-knowledge.
By means of these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and attain all-knowledge.

"Just as the former Śākyamuni Buddha sat beneath the Bodhi tree, dwelling in the inconceivable, stainless samādhi, subduing Māra, and regarding all dharmas that can be known, seen, and realized, at the time when the morning star appeared in the latter part of the night, attained the realization of the *amṛta* (the essence of nectar) through the practice of wisdom corresponding to a single thought-moment on the path to the cessation of suffering;
so too shall I do, for the sake of all sentient beings who study *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*."

Just as the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas—namely, the Tathāgata Immeasurable Radiance, the Tathāgata Supreme Radiance, the Tathāgata Pure Radiance, the Tathāgata Merit Radiance, the Tathāgata Lion, the Tathāgata Hundred Lights, the Tathāgata High Brilliance, the Tathāgata Net Light, the Tathāgata Jewel Light, the Tathāgata Fire Light, the Tathāgata King of Light, the Tathāgata Adorned, the Tathāgata Jewel Banner, the Tathāgata Dharma Banner, and the Tathāgata Supreme Body—as well as all other Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, who have already attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and have already turned the wheel of Dharma for the benefit of many sentient beings, for the peace and security of all sentient beings, out of compassion for the world, and even for the sake of benefiting all devas and humans through its meaning;

I am likewise: for the sake of all sentient beings attaining *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, I shall turn the wheel of Dharma, for the benefit of many beings, for the peace and security of beings, out of compassion for the world, and even to benefit all gods and humans through its meaning.
“Śāriputra! This is called the mass of merit from dedication.

This mass of merit surpasses the previous mass of merit from giving by a hundredfold, a thousandfold, ten-thousandfold, a hundred-thousandfold, a millionfold, ten-millionfold, a hundred-millionfold, a billionfold, ten-billionfold, a hundred-billionfold, a trillionfold, and even beyond what can be reached by calculation or analogy.”
“Śāriputra! If a son of good family or a daughter of good family receives, upholds, and extensively explains this sutra for others, the merit they obtain will be incalculable and immeasurable.”

Śāriputra! Suppose there were someone who could cause all the various classes of sentient beings in the trichiliocosm to simultaneously attain human bodies in a single thought-moment, and furthermore, could cause them all to attain the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha. Then, they would constantly provide these pratyekabuddhas with the four requisites of offering, bestowing upon each one seven precious jewels as vast as Mount Sumeru. This they would do day after day until those pratyekabuddhas entered parinirvāṇa; and once they had entered parinirvāṇa, they would erect stupas made of the seven precious jewels for them, making various offerings of flowers, incense, banners, and canopies.
"Śāriputra, what do you think? Is the merit obtained by these sons and daughters of good family not great? Śāriputra replied:
“Very much so, World-Honored One!
Very much so, Sugata! “Therefore, Śāriputra!”

If a son or daughter of good family receives and upholds this sutra, the merit they obtain will be even greater than that; may this merit lead to *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Compared to the former merit, this merit exceeds it by a hundredfold, a thousandfold, ten millionfold, a billionfold, and even beyond what can be reached by calculation or analogy.
Why is this? Śāriputra!

If good men and good women believe in this sutra and entreat the Buddhas of the ten directions to turn the wheel of Dharma, their gift of Dharma as I have taught it is superior to the gift of material wealth!

At that time, ten thousand people from the fourfold assembly rose from their seats together; they all bared their right shoulders, placed their right knees upon the ground, joined their palms toward the Buddha, and spoke these words:
"World-Honored One!
"We shall uphold this sutra and widely expound it for others; they should believe it.
Why is this? World-Honored One, we desire to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi!"
"I shall accomplish such roots of goodness and such wholesome dharmas!
At that time, Śakra, King of the Devas, scattered celestial flowers as an offering to the World-Honored One and to this Dharma of the sutra, and spoke these words:
"World-Honored One!..."
"This sutra possesses great merit; it serves to increase the roots of goodness of all bodhisattvas and to extinguish karmic obstructions.
At that time, the Buddha said to Śakra: "So it is, so it is!"
Kauśika! Why is this? O Devendra!
I recall that in the past, incalculable eons ago, at that time there appeared in the world the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Mahāprabhāskandha.
O Heavenly King!

The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Mahāprabhāsaṃcaya had a lifespan of sixty-eight billion years. When he first preached the Dharma, there were hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of disciples, all of whom were arhats who had exhausted all outflows (*āsrava*).
During his second preaching of the Dharma, there were ninety-nine thousand billion disciples, all of whom likewise exhausted their outflows and attained arhatship.
During his third preaching of the Dharma, there were ninety-eight billion hundred thousand disciples, whose outflows were already exhausted and who had attained arhatship.
"O Heavenly King!
That Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, the Great Mass of Radiance, remained for sixty-eight hundred million years for the sake of all the devas, Brahmās, śramaṇas, and brāhmaṇas in all the worlds."

At that time, Śakra, King of Devas, and the fourfold assembly received and upheld this sutra from the Tathāgata Raśmisaṃcaya, for the great benefit of all the world and for the sake of attaining anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Furthermore, there was a goddess named Kākatī who, having upheld this sutra and resolved her mind upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, grew weary of and detached from her female form, attained a male body, and was constantly reborn among humans and devas without passing through the evil realms; for eighty-four thousand lifetimes, she served as a wheel-turning monarch.
Kauśika! What do you think? Is that woman Gārgī here someone other than myself?
She is indeed my very self.

In the past, throughout hundreds of thousands of millions of worlds, I encountered countless Buddhas, all named Tathāgata Prabhāsa-rāśi; in the presence of those Buddhas, I heard this sutra in its entirety.
If good sons or good daughters hear the name of this Tathāgata, they will certainly attain Great Parinirvāṇa.

If there are women who hear the name of this Tathāgata Prabhāsa-rāśi, they shall transform their female bodies; at the end of their lives, they will be free from confusion and doubt, and shall never again receive a female body.
Kauśika! The great merit and grace of this sutra can sustain the roots of goodness of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and can extinguish all karmic obstructions.
At that time, Śakra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One,
what should this sutra be named?"
"How should it be received and upheld?
At that time, the Buddha told Śakra: "Kauśika!"
This sutra is titled "The Extinction of Obstructions of Karma"; you should uphold it.
It is also titled "The Bodhisattva-piṭaka"; you should uphold it.
It is also titled "The Severing of All Doubts"; you should uphold it in this way.

When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, Śakra, the King of Devas, the Elder Śāriputra, the assembly of bhikṣus, and all the bodhisattvas, devas, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and the entire world, having heard what the Buddha taught, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
